Before you send a single marketing text, you need explicit written consent.
The Telephone Consumer Protection Act requires it.
Getting opt-in right is the foundation the whole system sits on.
A checkbox at checkout with clear disclosure language.
A keyword opt-in where the customer texts a word to your number.
Or a paper sign-up sheet at the counter for service businesses where the customer is on-site.
The first message goes out same day or next morning.
This message generates replies 20 to 30 percent of the time.
Every reply is a chance to solve a problem before it becomes a negative review.
Message two fires on day three or four with a specific offer.
Come back soon does not.
Give them a concrete reason with a loose deadline.
The third message fires at day 28 to 30.
A customer who had a good experience a month ago and has not been contacted since is far more likely to rebook.
You are reminding someone who already chose you.
Opt-out rates stay below 2 percent when businesses send four or fewer texts per month.
The 3-message sequence keeps you well within that range.
More than that and opt-out rates climb fast, damaging your list permanently.
